newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Palestinians want U.N. reconvened on settlements.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians want U.N. reconvened on settlements.

text.p: A Palestinian spokesman accused Israel on Tuesday of exploiting occupied Palestinian territory for the past 30 years and said an emergency special session of the General Assembly on Israel's settlement policies should be reconvened.
Saeb Erekat, minister for local government in the Palestinian self-rule authority, also said Israel's nuclear programme threatened the region with a "dangerous environmental disaster."
He was addressing an Earth Summit that is reviewing progress since the 1992 U.N. environment conference in Rio de Janeiro. The Palestine Liberation Organisation has U.N. observer status.

Erekat said Israel, as the occupying power for the past 30 years had "exploited the natural resources of the occupied Palestinian territory, including Jerusalem, and confiscated land and uprooted trees."

Erekat also accused Israel of using Palestinian territory as "a backyard to dispose of its waste" and said Israel's nuclear programme, not subject to international supervision, "threatens the region with a dangerous environmental disaster, in addition to the fact that its possession of nuclear weapons will force the region into a destructive nuclear race."

He said Israel obstructed the dispatch of a U.N. mission under a resolution adopted by the emergency Assembly session, which called for a halt to the construction of an Israeli settlement in East Jerusalem, asking Secretary-General Kofi Annan to monitor the situation and submit a report within two months.
Erekat said the Israeli action was a "flagrant defiance of the will of the international community" and weakened efforts to achieve stability and peace in the Middle East.
"In this context, we will request the resumption of the 10th emergency special session to review the report of the secretary-general," he said.

The emergency session was adjourned temporarily but authorised to resume at the request of U.N. members. A 1980 special Assembly session on the question of Palestine was resumed four times during 1982.
